skill.name: api-testing-observability-api-mock
skill.description: Guides creation of realistic API mock services for development, testing, demos, contract validation, scenario simulation, and synthetic data generation.
skill.summary: Build contract-aware mock APIs with scenarios, fixtures, performance profiles, and test integration guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are documentation false positives: localhost calls, sample request handlers, dictionary configuration access, and Markdown backticks. I confirmed low-risk external CDN references in the interactive documentation template and added a low-severity semantic finding for full request-header capture in mock tracking. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious command execution.

remediation.issue: External Swagger UI assets are loaded from unpinned unpkg URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact asset versions or package Swagger UI locally before publishing generated documentation.

remediation.issue: The request tracking sample stores all request headers.
remediation.suggestion: Redact Authorization, Cookie, and similar secret-bearing headers before storing mock request history.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Sensitive Header Retention in Mock Request Tracking
semantic_findings.description: The mock server sample records full request headers in the state manager. If users test with real Authorization or Cookie values, the mock history can retain sensitive data locally.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code sample stores dict(request.headers), which can include secret-bearing headers. The skill also warns against production secrets, so this is a bounded hardening issue rather than malicious behavior.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable API behavior before services or partners are available. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create contract-aware mocks, scenarios, fixtures, tests, and deployment notes.
actual_capabilities: Designs FastAPI-style mock server routes, middleware, request matching, and response stubs.
Creates success, authentication, validation, rate limit, and unavailable service scenarios.
Generates synthetic fixtures from schemas with deterministic controls and optional randomness.
Outlines contract validation, test integration, Docker deployment, and interactive documentation patterns.
Provides latency, throughput, error rate, and response size simulation guidance.
Describes request tracking and metrics collection for mock verification.
limitations: Does not test production systems or live integrations.
Requires an API contract, expected behavior, or representative endpoint examples.
Generated samples need dependency review before deployment.
Mock request tracking should be configured to avoid storing sensitive headers.

use_cases.title: Parallel Frontend Development
use_cases.description: Frontend teams can build against stable mock endpoints while backend APIs are incomplete.

use_cases.title: Partner API Simulation
use_cases.description: Integration engineers can reproduce partner responses, error states, and latency without calling external services.

use_cases.title: Demo Environment Setup
use_cases.description: Product teams can create predictable demo data and scenarios for sales, onboarding, and stakeholder reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Mock
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design mock endpoints for [API name]. Include routes, sample responses, error cases, and run instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Model Test Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define happy path, auth failure, validation error, rate limit, and unavailable service scenarios for [workflow].

prompt_templates.title: Generate Contract-Based Mocks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill with this OpenAPI summary: [summary]. Produce route mappings, fixture rules, validation checks, and test integration notes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Stateful Mock Platform
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a stateful mock service for [system]. Include scenario switching, data relationships, latency profiles, deployment, and observability.

output_examples.input: Design a mock user profile API for frontend testing.
output: A route list for profile lookup, profile update, avatar upload, and preferences.
Synthetic user fixtures with stable identifiers and repeatable values.
Error scenarios for missing users, validation failures, and expired sessions.

output_examples.input: Create failure scenarios for a payments integration.
output: A scenario matrix covering approved payment, declined card, expired token, rate limit, and provider outage.
Expected status codes, user-facing error messages, and retry guidance for each scenario.
Test notes for switching scenarios without calling the payment provider.

output_examples.input: Plan deployment for a demo mock API.
output: A deployment checklist for local Docker use and shared demo environments.
Configuration notes for mock data paths, scenario selection, and health checks.
Documentation guidance so users can identify mock endpoints clearly.

best_practices: Start with the API contract, then define route behavior, status codes, and error shapes.
Use synthetic data only, and label every mock endpoint clearly.
Keep scenario names stable so tests and demos can switch behavior predictably.
anti_patterns: Do not connect mock services to production systems or real customer data.
Do not hide random behavior inside tests without a repeatable seed or scenario switch.
Do not treat generated sample code as deployment-ready without dependency review.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps design realistic mock APIs, fixtures, scenarios, contract checks, and deployment notes for development and testing.

faq.question: Does it call live APIs?
faq.answer: No. The skill is intended for mock services and should not be used to test production systems.

faq.question: Can it work from an OpenAPI contract?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide route mapping, response generation, validation, and tests from contract details.

faq.question: Can it model errors and latency?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for error scenarios, rate limits, service outages, latency, throughput, and response sizes.

faq.question: Is generated data real customer data?
faq.answer: No. Mock data should be synthetic, clearly labeled, and reviewed before sharing.

faq.question: What should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide endpoints, request fields, response shapes, auth behavior, scenario needs, and expected latency ranges.
